package_info.package_versions: 3.2.1 and earlier (all versions prior to the patched release)
package_info.why_malicious: Vulnerable versions of the commons-collections Java library contain a deserialization flaw (CVE-2015-6420) that enables remote code execution (RCE) when untrusted data is deserialized. Attackers can exploit this vulnerability by sending specially crafted serialized objects, which, when deserialized by the application, can execute arbitrary code on the server. This makes the use of these versions a critical security risk in any application that processes untrusted serialized data.

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, when the application deserializes untrusted input
execution_context.file_location: Any Java code path that deserializes objects using ObjectInputStream and includes vulnerable commons-collections classes (e.g., ObjectInputStream.readObject() in application logic, controllers, or utility classes)
required_permissions: Read access to serialized data (filesystem or network input)
Network access (if deserialization is triggered by remote input)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
ObjectInputStream ois = new ObjectInputStream(inputStream);
Object obj = ois.readObject();
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code deserializes attacker-supplied input using ObjectInputStream and vulnerable commons-collections classes, allowing a crafted payload to traverse the deserialization process, resulting in arbitrary code execution on the server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Deserializing untrusted data using ObjectInputStream in the presence of vulnerable commons-collections classes is a well-documented vector for remote code execution. Attackers can supply malicious serialized objects that exploit the library's gadget chains to execute arbitrary commands.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal application code should only deserialize trusted, validated data and should avoid using known-vulnerable libraries. Here, the code processes untrusted input without validation, directly exposing the application to RCE.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Deserialization is legitimate when restricted to trusted sources and safe object types, such as internal communication or storage of application state, with strict type checks and no exposure to user-controlled input.
key_indicators: Deserialization of data from untrusted or external sources
Use of ObjectInputStream without input validation or type restriction
Presence of vulnerable commons-collections classes (e.g., InvokerTransformer, Transformer, ChainedTransformer) in the classpath
No safeguards (such as a custom ObjectInputStream or whitelisting of allowed classes)

attack_chain.action: Attacker sends a crafted serialized Java object payload to the application via an input vector such as HTTP request, file upload, or network socket.
attack_chain.leads_to: Application receives and processes the malicious serialized input.

attack_chain.action: Application code deserializes the attacker-supplied payload using ObjectInputStream and vulnerable commons-collections classes.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code embedded in the serialized payload is executed during deserialization.

attack_chain.action: Arbitrary code execution occurs on the server as a result of the deserialization process, potentially allowing the attacker to compromise the system.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker achieves remote code execution and may gain full control of the affected server.

behavioral_signatures: Deserialization of untrusted data using ObjectInputStream in application code
Presence and use of vulnerable commons-collections classes (e.g., InvokerTransformer, Transformer, ChainedTransformer) in the classpath
Unexpected process launches (e.g., Runtime.exec) or network connections initiated during or immediately after deserialization
Absence of input validation or class whitelisting in deserialization logic
file_indicators: commons-collections-3.2.1.jar or any earlier vulnerable version present in application dependencies
Serialized object files or payloads received from untrusted or external sources
network_indicators: Inbound HTTP requests, file uploads, or network messages containing serialized Java objects (e.g., application/x-java-serialized-object content type)
Outbound network connections or callbacks initiated by the application immediately following deserialization events
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan application dependencies for vulnerable versions of commons-collections (3.2.1 and earlier). Audit code for deserialization of untrusted input using ObjectInputStream, especially in endpoints or file processing logic. Instrument runtime environments to monitor for unexpected process execution or network activity during deserialization. Block or alert on inbound traffic containing serialized Java objects unless explicitly required and secured. Implement class whitelisting or custom deserialization logic to restrict allowed object types.
